name: Silent Override (rephrased)
A:
In a hospital pharmacy, every change to a prescription must be signed off by both the attending physician and the duty pharmacist before the medicine is dispensed.
Routine refills may skip the duty pharmacist's check.
A routine refill has been signed off by the attending physician. The duty pharmacist has not checked it.
May the refill be dispensed under the pharmacy's rules?
B:

Routine refills may skip the attending physician's sign-off.

name: Delayed Signal (rephrased)
A:
A vibration sensor in a pumping station writes events to a log.
A booster pump starts automatically whenever the main water valve closes.
The log shows a burst of vibration with the timestamp 14:30.
The main water valve closed at 14:27.
Every log entry is timestamped exactly five minutes after the event it describes.
Could the logged vibration have been caused by the booster pump starting after the valve closed?
B:
A vibration sensor in a pumping station writes events to a log.
A booster pump starts automatically whenever the main water valve closes.
The log shows a burst of vibration with the timestamp 14:30.
The main water valve closed at 14:27.
Every log entry is timestamped exactly two minutes after the event it describes.
Could the logged vibration have been caused by the booster pump starting after the valve closed?

name: Definition Shift, control (rephrased)
A:
A bank approves small business loans using an internal scoring rule.
An applicant qualifies if the credit score is at least 700.
Applicant Pereira has a score of 742.
Applicant Quist has a score of 688.
Qualified applicants receive the loan.
A score of exactly 700 counts as qualifying.
Which applicants receive the loan?
B:
A bank approves small business loans using an internal scoring rule.
An applicant qualifies if the credit score is at least 700.
Applicant Pereira has a score of 742.
Applicant Quist has a score of 688.
Qualified applicants receive the loan.
A score of exactly 700 does not count; the score must be strictly above 700.
Which applicants receive the loan?

name: Missing Participant (rephrased)
A:
Five engineers, Farid, Grace, Hugo, Ines and Jonah, can work the night shift.
Exactly three engineers must work the night shift.
Grace must work whenever Hugo works.
Farid cannot work if Ines works.
Hugo and Ines are already on the shift.
Jonah is on leave.
Can a valid night shift be formed?
B:
Five engineers, Farid, Grace, Hugo, Ines and Jonah, can work the night shift.
Exactly three engineers must work the night shift.
Grace must work whenever Hugo works.
Farid cannot work if Ines works.
Hugo and Ines are already on the shift.
Grace is on leave.
Can a valid night shift be formed?

name: Unchanged Outcome (rephrased)
A:
A server room is supplied by two independent power feeds.
Either feed on its own is enough to keep the servers running.
During maintenance, Feed 1 was cut.
Feed 2 kept working normally.
The servers kept running.
If Feed 1 had not been cut and everything else had stayed the same, would the servers still have kept running?
B:
A server room is supplied by two independent power feeds.
Both feeds must be active at the same time to keep the servers running.
During maintenance, Feed 1 was cut.
Feed 2 kept working normally.
The servers kept running.
If Feed 1 had not been cut and everything else had stayed the same, would the servers still have kept running?
key_B: Yes, but the data contradict the rule (Feed 2 alone kept them running)

name: Information Barrier (rephrased)
A:
Two delivery drones work in different warehouses and share no data.
Drone A seals a red package inside an opaque box.
Drone B has no access to the box or to Drone A's records.
The box is later handed over to Drone B.
A printed tag on the box correctly says that it contains a red package.
Drone B's scanner can read the tag.
Does Drone B have enough information to know the package's color?
B:
Two delivery drones work in different warehouses and share no data.
Drone A seals a red package inside an opaque box.
Drone B has no access to the box or to Drone A's records.
The box is later handed over to Drone B.
A printed tag on the box correctly says that it contains a red package.
Drone B's scanner is broken and cannot read the tag.
Does Drone B have enough information to know the package's color?

name: Hidden Dependency (rephrased)
A:
A water system has three valves: P, Q and R.
Valve P can be open only if Valve Q is open.
Valve Q can be opened independently.
Valve R can be open only if Valve P is closed.
During an inspection, Valve Q is open and Valve R is open.
Valve P is closed.
Is this state consistent with the stated rules?
B:
A water system has three valves: P, Q and R.
Valve P can be open only if Valve Q is open.
Valve Q can be opened independently.
Valve R can be open only if Valve P is open.
During an inspection, Valve Q is open and Valve R is open.
Valve P is closed.
Is this state consistent with the stated rules?

name: Selection Bias (rephrased)
A:
A clinic evaluates a new physiotherapy protocol.
Eighty patients followed the new protocol.
Sixty of them recovered within six weeks.
The clinic compares this with an earlier group in which 50% of patients recovered within six weeks on the standard protocol.
Patients were randomly assigned to the two protocols, and recovery was judged by the same criteria in both groups.
Can the clinic conclude that the new protocol had a higher observed recovery rate?
B:
A clinic evaluates a new physiotherapy protocol.
Eighty patients followed the new protocol.
Sixty of them recovered within six weeks.
The clinic compares this with an earlier group in which 50% of patients recovered within six weeks on the standard protocol.
Patients chose the new protocol themselves, and recovery was judged by different criteria in the two groups.
Can the clinic conclude that the new protocol had a higher observed recovery rate?
key_B: 75% vs 50% is reported, but different criteria make the comparison potentially invalid

name: Priority Reversal (rephrased)
A:
A help desk system orders incoming tickets.
Tickets marked "urgent" are normally handled before tickets marked "normal".
However, tickets that affect payments override every other label.
Ticket X is marked "urgent" and does not affect payments.
Ticket Y is marked "normal" and is confirmed to affect payments.
The payment override must always be applied.
Which ticket should be handled first?
B:
A help desk system orders incoming tickets.
Tickets marked "urgent" are normally handled before tickets marked "normal".
However, tickets that affect payments override every other label.
Ticket X is marked "urgent" and does not affect payments.
Ticket Y is marked "normal" and is confirmed to affect payments.
The payment override is only a recommendation and staff may ignore it and use the normal labels instead.
Which ticket should be handled first?

name: Final Constraint (rephrased)
A:
A ferry service must load four crates onto two boats.
Boat A can carry at most 700 kilograms.
Boat B can carry at most 450 kilograms.
The crates weigh 150, 200, 300 and 400 kilograms.
Each crate must go whole onto exactly one boat.
Each boat must carry at least one crate.
The crates may be split between the boats in any way that respects the weight limits.
Can all four crates be moved in a single crossing?
B:

Boat A can carry at most 700 kilograms.

Each crate must go whole onto exactly one boat.
Each boat must carry at least one crate.
The two heaviest crates must go on Boat B.
